title: Z-Privesc evaluation corpus
description: Manifest of labelled evaluation targets. Each target plants one or more known misconfigurations (via a setup script) and declares ground truth plus exploit-verification procedures used to fit and test the composition engine's calibrated reliability weights.

id.description: Unique target identifier. Results are written under <results>/<id>/.

setup.description: Path (relative to repo root) to a setup script run as root on the target to plant the misconfiguration.

teardown.description: Path to a cleanup script run as root to remove the plant.

verify.description: Exploit-verification procedures. Each produces one calibration outcome (label, p, y).

reachable_tokens.description: Privilege tokens (see src/compose.c T_* enum names) reachable on this target.

expected_paths.description: Expected escalation_path 'technique' strings, e.g. 'WRITE_SUDOERS -> root'. Used for path-level recall/precision.

expected_findings.description: Finding id signatures expected to appear in Z-Privesc output (detection recall).

root_reachable.description: True if the target should yield at least one 'X -> root' path. Defaults to (expected_paths non-empty).

label.description: Calibration key. MUST equal either (a) a rule 'tech' string in src/compose.c RULES[] (e.g. 'execute code as root'), or (b) a privilege token name (e.g. 'ROOT') for direct grants with no composing rule.

kind.description: Whether this verifies a whole escalation path (path) or a single composing rule/step (step). Both yield one calibration outcome keyed by 'label'.

check.description: Shell command run as 'as_user'. MUST return exit 0 IF AND ONLY IF the escalation to root (or the step) genuinely succeeds. Ignored when manual=true.

as_user.description: Unprivileged user the check runs as (via 'sudo -u'). The exploit is expected to elevate this user to root.

manual.description: If true, 'check' is NOT executed; 'expected_y' is used as the verified outcome (human-verified, e.g. kernel LPE / polkit CVE where safe automated verification is impractical).
